title: Inference Playbook + Savings Sandbox — Batching & KV Cache Walkthrough
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-18 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes (scheduled)
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Links shared: https://redwood.app/sandbox/emerald-sim (cost sim), https://redwood.app/docs/optimize (docs)

Summary:
Quick Optimize walkthrough of batching + prefix/KV cache recommendations with a small savings sandbox demo. Goal: validate cost estimates for Emerald's chat product (short sessions, heavy context), identify quick wins for 30-40% unit-cost reduction without breaking latency SLOs.

Topics covered:
- workload profile: short interactive sessions vs long context pass-through
- batching strategies (concurrency, dynamic batching windows)
- prefix and KV caching tradeoffs for sessionization
- prefetch heuristics and TTLs
- dedicated vs hosted model routing in fallbacks
- security/compliance notes (VPC, KMS, SOC2)

Action items (captured in call; duplicates listed in metadata):
- Marcus to run a 10k request simulation with Emerald sample traces and share spreadsheet by Mon 1/24
- Lena to share pricing ballpark and sandbox access link
- Emerald to confirm top-5 user flows and expected latency SLOs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): ok hey everyone thanks for coming on time. this is lena from Redwood, ive got marcus (se) with me, he's going to run through the savings sandbox and the playbook. how's everyone doing?
[00:09] Ravi (Emerald CTO): good, thanks. excited to see how we can squeeze costs. we are running a chat product with lots of short sessions, average tokens is like 180 per session but we sometimes attach a 5k context for retrieval.
[00:23] Marcus (Redwood SE): cool, yeah that pattern is a great candidate for prefix and kv caching. quick note, sometimes the auto transcriber turns KV to "KV cash" so ignore that if you see it later.
[00:33] Maya (ML Lead): haha, ok noted. our big worry is hitting the 200ms P95 for the UI, and we cannot increase latency much.
[00:40] Jonas (VP Eng): and we have strict data residency — EU region, plus we'd like to keep customer logs off the hosted service if possible.
[00:48] Marcus: understood. i'll show two sandbox scenarios: first a hosted path with aggressive prefix caching and batching tuned for very low unit-cost, second a dedicated pool scenario where we trade some cost for more predictable tail latency.
[00:58] Lena: i'll quick-flag compliance stuff — we have SOC2 docs and can integrate KMS for key management in Private; i'll drop links after the call.
[01:06] Marcus: ok demo slide 1, workload breakdown. (screen share) so your session histogram — lots at 30-200 tokens, a smaller mode with 3-5k retrieval tokens. This suggests a hybrid strategy: prefix caching for the repeated short sessions, and selective prefetch for the long retrievals.
[01:29] Marcus: batching — we recommend targeting concurrency of 8-16 for your API layer with a dynamic batching window: 10-20ms micro-window then flush, this gives good throughput without adding >10-20ms median latency. the sandbox sim models 1k qps for 5 minutes with that config.
[01:47] Maya: hmm 10-20ms window sounds fine if p95 stays under 200ms, do you have the p95 numbers?
[01:53] Marcus: yeah in the hosted sim with prefix cache hit-rate at 60% we see p50 ~85ms, p95 ~170ms, cost per session drops ~36% vs no-cache baseline. note these numbers vary with sequence length and model variant.
[02:12] Ravi: what about KV prefetch TTLs? we can't keep everything in cache for long because of memory on the hosted pool.
[02:18] Marcus: good question — we recommend a two-tier TTL: short TTL of 30s-2m for highly active sessions and a cold TTL of 10-30m for low-touch sessions. the simulator uses a heatmap to allocate cache keys — you can tune by percentiles. for your workload i suggested initial short TTL 90s and cold TTL 15m.
[02:38] Jonas: are those TTLs configurable per customer? we need to enforce per-tenant quotas.
[02:42] Lena: yes per-tenant limits and RBAC are supported, you can set memory caps and eviction policy via the console.
[02:49] Marcus: also important: prefix caching stores KV entries of model kv for common prefixes — that reduces token compute because we skip recomputing early layers. it can cut compute by up to 40% for repeated prompts.
[03:05] Maya: do you have an example where prefix cache hurts accuracy? like when the prompt changes slightly?
[03:10] Marcus: yes, prefix cache can be brittle if prompts mutate semantically; we profile prompt variance and only cache when similarity > 0.85 in the sandbox. when similarity drops we bypass cache automatically.
[03:23] Ravi: ok and how does fallback work if cache misses spike during peak? we can't have huge error rates.
[03:28] Marcus: routing policy: primary is hosted low-cost variant, fallback to dedicated pool or model-quantized variant. you can set a fallback policy based on latency or error rate. we also support circuit-breaker style auto-fallback when queue depth crosses threshold.
[03:44] Jonas: you mentioned quantized variants — do those degrade quality significantly?
[03:47] Marcus: depends on model; for many open models 4-bit quantization with proper calibration has minimal delta on top-n accuracy for typical chat tasks. in the sandbox sims we show BLEU-ish proxies and human eval flags for regression.
[04:02] Maya: i want to see the cost sim results end-to-end for our traffic shape.
[04:06] Marcus: sure, switch to the savings sandbox sheet. (shared) this sheet has three scenarios: baseline no-cache, prefix-only, prefix+kv+batching. each row is Monte Carlo of different hit rates and concurrency.
[04:22] Marcus: for Emerald's profile, prefix-only yields ~22% savings, combined approach yields median ~39% savings, 90th percentile ~31% depending on prefetch accuracy.
[04:33] Ravi: those look promising. what's the engineering lift to get to prefix+KV?
[04:38] Lena: typical integration is: instrument request traces (we provide SDK hooks), run sample traces through the cost sim, then enable sandbox with limited traffic for 2 weeks. Marcus can do a POC run.
[04:50] Marcus: lift-wise, work items: integrate the SDK (30-60 developer hours), define prefetch keys and TTLs (design session heuristics), test in staging, then enable in canary. exact hours depend on your infra and SSO setup.
[05:06] Jonas: what about region/residency — if we need EU only, can we run everything in the EU hosted region or do we need Private?
[05:13] Marcus: we have hosted EU regions with data-in-region guarantees, logs can be redacted at request so you can keep PII off the hosted logs. if you need full control — e.g., no third-party logs — you can run Redwood Private in your VPC or on-prem.
[05:27] Ravi: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys?
[05:30] Lena: yes we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated; hosted supports envelope encryption with customer KMS for keys. i'll send the KMS integration doc.
[05:39] Maya: quick nit — do you account for network egress in the sim?
[05:42] Marcus: we include a network cost line item but it's typically small vs GPU. for large retrieval contexts the egress can climb — that is visible in the sheet.
[05:51] (short pause)
[05:54] Marcus: ok demo two, dedicated pool behaviour. if you want tighter tail latency we reserve GPU pools and can pin capacity. this costs more per-hour but reduces variance and gives predictable throughput. in the sim dedicated reduces p95 variance by ~40%.
[06:10] Ravi: is burst capacity possible? we have marketing spikes.
[06:14] Marcus: yes autoscale burst: you can configure a burst buffer that borrows from spare capacity for short periods; we also have an overflow to compatible cheaper models if needed.
[06:24] Jonas: security checklist — can we get the SOC2/SSO docs asap for procurement?
[06:29] Lena: absolutely, i'll attach SOC2, SSO/SAML guide, and the Private deployment checklist in the follow-up email.
[06:37] Maya: what about cost attribution per token per route? we need that for finance.
[06:41] Marcus: Console exposes token-level cost breakdown and you can tag requests by tenant and route; the sandboxes include a per-route costing column so finance can attribute spend.
[06:51] Ravi: ok next steps?
[06:53] Lena: recap: Marcus will run a 10k-request sim with Emerald traces and share the workbook; Lena will send SOC2, KMS, and sandbox access; Emerald will pick 5 flows and confirm latency SLOs; then schedule a two-hour POC scoping with infra.
[07:07] Jonas: timeline — can we aim for the sim results by next Monday?
[07:10] Marcus: yes i'll have sim results and a prefilled sheet by Mon 2027-01-24.
[07:14] Ravi: thanks all.
[07:16] Lena: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and invite for the scoping session.
[07:20] (recording ends)
